title: Primer: istio-ingress-gateway integration
description:
Write references/integrations/istio-ingress-gateway.md so the skill can generate scenarios that test exposing a consumer chart through an Istio ingress gateway. Distinct from the mesh primer: this tests NORTH-SOUTH traffic via the istio Gateway CR + VirtualService, not sidecar injection. The scenario installs istio + an ingressgateway, wires a Gateway+VirtualService pointing at the chart Service, and verifies external traffic reaches the backend through the gateway.

Follow the fixed 5-section primer shape (references/workflow.md phase 4); mirror cert-manager.md depth.
design: Cluster preinstall: istio/base + istio/istiod + istio/gateway (the ingressgateway, repo https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts), pinned ~1.21. Feasibility Required: pod-owning kind; chart exposes a Service (VirtualService route destination). Soft: chart exposes host/ingress values we can reuse for the VirtualService host. Values-override: enable chart Service; chartTestSwarm.enabled=true. Helm-test: create Gateway (selector istio=ingressgateway, port 80, host) + VirtualService (hosts + http route to the chart Service) via hook ConfigMap; then curl the ingressgateway Service (port-forward or NodePort on kind) with the right Host header and assert 200. Common failure modes: Gateway selector doesn't match the ingressgateway pod labels; VirtualService host mismatch with curl Host header; ingressgateway not reachable on kind without port-forward/NodePort; gateway CRD vs Gateway-API CRD name collision (istio Gateway is networking.istio.io, NOT gateway.networking.k8s.io — call this out explicitly to avoid confusion with the gateway-api primer).
acceptance_criteria: references/integrations/istio-ingress-gateway.md exists with all 5 H2 sections; explicitly disambiguates istio Gateway (networking.istio.io) from Gateway API (gateway.networking.k8s.io); helm-test curls through the gateway and asserts 200; gated behind chartTestSwarm.enabled.

title: Primer: istio-service-mesh integration
description:
Write references/integrations/istio-service-mesh.md so the skill can generate scenarios that test a consumer chart inside an Istio service mesh with automatic sidecar injection. The scenario installs istio base + istiod, labels the target namespace istio-injection=enabled (or sets the sidecar.istio.io/inject pod annotation), installs the chart, and verifies every workload pod gets an istio-proxy sidecar that becomes Ready, plus mTLS works.

Follow the fixed 5-section primer shape (references/workflow.md phase 4); mirror cert-manager.md depth. This is the deepest-feasibility integration — sidecar injection has real chart requirements.
design: Cluster preinstall: istio/base (repo https://istio-release.storage.googleapis.com/charts) then istio/istiod, both pinned (~1.21). wait pods-ready on istiod. Namespace gets label istio-injection=enabled (apply via fixture or the run sets it). Feasibility Required: pod-owning kind; NO hostNetwork (host_network must be false — hostNetwork pods bypass the sidecar); container ports are named with a protocol prefix OR appProtocol set (istio needs http-/grpc- port name prefixes for L7 features — surface as Soft if not). Soft: pod annotations value-driven (so we can add sidecar.istio.io/inject or traffic.sidecar.istio.io annotations); pod labels value-driven; readiness probe present (sidecar can race app startup — holdApplicationUntilProxyStarts helps). Values-override: ensure namespace injection or set pod annotation sidecar.istio.io/inject=true via the chart's podAnnotations knob; chartTestSwarm.enabled=true. Helm-test: (1) assert the chart's pod has 2+ containers including istio-proxy (kubectl get pod -o jsonpath containers); (2) assert istio-proxy container is Ready; (3) optionally apply a STRICT PeerAuthentication and curl between two pods to prove mTLS. Common failure modes: pod stuck PodInitializing because istio-init waits on istio-cni (the exact failure already seeded in the demo data!); hostNetwork pods silently un-meshed; unnamed ports degrade to TCP-only; sidecar OOM on tiny limits; job/cronjob pods never complete because sidecar keeps running (needs holdApplicationUntilProxyStarts + exit hook).
acceptance_criteria: references/integrations/istio-service-mesh.md exists with all 5 H2 sections; Required checklist includes no-hostNetwork; helm-test verifies sidecar present AND ready; documents the istio-init/CNI failure mode; gated behind chartTestSwarm.enabled.

title: Primer: opa-gatekeeper integration
description:
Write references/integrations/opa-gatekeeper.md so the skill can generate scenarios that test whether a consumer chart's workloads SURVIVE common OPA Gatekeeper admission policies. Unlike the ingress/cert integrations (which add capability), gatekeeper REMOVES capability — it rejects non-compliant pods at admission. The scenario installs Gatekeeper + a set of representative ConstraintTemplates+Constraints (required labels, disallow privileged, require resource limits, disallow :latest tag), then installs the chart and asserts its pods are ADMITTED (not denied).

Follow the fixed 5-section primer shape (references/workflow.md phase 4); mirror cert-manager.md depth.
design: Cluster preinstall: gatekeeper helm chart (repo https://open-policy-agent.github.io/gatekeeper/charts, chart gatekeeper). Then apply a bundle of ConstraintTemplates + Constraints via hook/fixture: K8sRequiredLabels, K8sPSPPrivilegedContainer (disallow privileged), K8sContainerLimits (require cpu/mem limits), K8sDisallowedTags (block :latest). Feasibility Required: pod-owning kind. Soft (these are what gatekeeper will reject if missing — surface as caveats, NOT hard-fails, because the POINT is to discover non-compliance): pod securityContext configurable in values; resource limits present/configurable; image tag is pinned (not latest); pod labels configurable. Values-override: set the chart's resource limits + securityContext + required labels to COMPLIANT values; chartTestSwarm.enabled=true. Helm-test: (1) assert the chart's own pods reached Running (proves admission passed); (2) attempt to create a deliberately-violating bare pod and assert Gatekeeper DENIES it (proves policies are actually enforcing, not failing open). Common failure modes: gatekeeper webhook not ready (fails open — pods admitted but policy not actually tested); audit vs enforcement mode confusion; constraint match selectors too narrow to catch the chart's namespace; chart hardcodes :latest or omits limits -> legitimately fails, report as a chart finding not a harness bug.
acceptance_criteria: references/integrations/opa-gatekeeper.md exists with all 5 H2 sections; checklist distinguishes hard Required from Soft compliance items; helm-test verifies BOTH admit-compliant AND deny-violating; gated behind chartTestSwarm.enabled.

title: Primer: traefik integration
description:
Write references/integrations/traefik.md so the skill can generate scenarios that test a consumer chart behind a Traefik ingress. Traefik can route via standard Ingress objects OR its own IngressRoute CRD (with Middleware, entryPoints, TLS). The scenario installs Traefik, points a route at the chart's Service, and verifies traffic flows through Traefik to the backend.

Follow the fixed 5-section primer shape (references/workflow.md phase 4); mirror cert-manager.md depth.
design: Cluster preinstall: traefik helm chart (repo https://traefik.github.io/charts, chart traefik). Pin version. On kind, expose via NodePort or rely on port-forward in the helm test. Feasibility Required: pod-owning kind; chart exposes a Service. Soft: chart exposes ingress.enabled / ingress annotations in values (lets us attach Traefik via annotations instead of a separate IngressRoute). Values-override: enable chart Service; if chart supports Ingress, set ingressClassName=traefik + host; chartTestSwarm.enabled=true. Helm-test: create an IngressRoute (or Ingress) via hook ConfigMap targeting the chart Service, then curl through the Traefik entrypoint and assert 200. Optionally test a Middleware (e.g. stripPrefix) to prove middleware compatibility. Common failure modes: IngressRoute CRD absent if Traefik installed with CRDs disabled; entrypoint not reachable on kind; class mismatch (traefik vs nginx); host header routing requires Host header in curl.
acceptance_criteria: references/integrations/traefik.md exists with all 5 H2 sections in order; Required+Soft checklist; drives a verdict against the sample chart; helm-test gated behind chartTestSwarm.enabled.

title: Primer: gateway-api integration
description:
Write references/integrations/gateway-api.md so the skill can generate scenarios that test a consumer chart against Kubernetes Gateway API (the standard successor to Ingress). Gateway API works via CRDs: GatewayClass, Gateway (the listener), and HTTPRoute (routing rules with parentRefs back to the Gateway). The consumer chart provides a Service; the scenario wires an HTTPRoute pointing at it and verifies traffic flows through the Gateway listener.

Follow the fixed 5-section primer shape (see references/workflow.md phase 4) and mirror the depth/voice of references/integrations/cert-manager.md.
design: Cluster preinstall: install Gateway API CRDs (kubectl apply the standard-install.yaml from gateway-api releases) + a controller that implements them — recommend nginx-gateway-fabric helm chart (repo oci://ghcr.io/nginxinc/charts/nginx-gateway-fabric) OR istio. Pin versions. Feasibility checklist Required: chart has a pod-owning kind; chart exposes a Service (HTTPRoute needs a backendRef target); Soft: chart exposes ingress/route toggles in values so we don't fork. Values-override: enable the chart's own Service; chartTestSwarm.enabled=true. Helm-test: create GatewayClass+Gateway+HTTPRoute (via hook ConfigMap like cert-manager primer does), then curl the Gateway listener address and assert 200 from the chart's backend. Common failure modes: CRDs not installed (no matches for kind HTTPRoute); controller not ready; listener port not allocated on kind (needs NodePort or port-forward); backendRef Service port name mismatch.
acceptance_criteria: references/integrations/gateway-api.md exists with all 5 H2 sections in order; feasibility checklist has Required + Soft subsections; primer drives a verdict against examples/sample-product-chart (expect IMPOSSIBLE-or-CAVEATS given the bare sample); helm-test pattern is gated behind .Values.chartTestSwarm.enabled.

title: Epic: codify remaining integration primers (v2-D)
description: The chart-test-swarm skill generates integration-test scenarios driven by per-integration primer files at engine/skills/chart-test-swarm/references/integrations/<name>.md. Only cert-manager.md exists. The SKILL.md frontmatter names 5 more (gateway-api, traefik, opa-gatekeeper, istio-service-mesh, istio-ingress-gateway) as roadmap, but without a primer each returns 'unsupported' at workflow phase 4. This epic ports all 5 into codified primers so the skill actually supports what it advertises. Reference implementation: references/integrations/cert-manager.md. Fixed primer shape is documented in references/workflow.md phase 4.
acceptance_criteria: All 5 primers exist, each conforming to the fixed 5-section shape; ls references/integrations/ shows 6 total; each primer drives a feasibility verdict against examples/sample-product-chart without error.
